stem.en: Kabir asks why they "could not just look and see what went in". What made the labels necessary?

text.en: Nothing in 1952 could see a molecule enter a cell. The label turns an invisible molecule into a countable glow, and the choice of sulphur versus phosphorus means each glow can only be one molecule. The detective tool from Book I.
They could have looked; they were lazy.

feedback.en: A microscope of the time showed the virus as a dot on the bacterium, and nothing of what passed between them.

text.en: The labels made the virus infect.

feedback.en: Unlabelled viruses infect exactly the same way. The label only makes one part visible.

text.en: They were checking whether the virus was radioactive.

feedback.en: They made it radioactive on purpose, to follow it. The question was which part went where.

explanation.en: When you cannot see a thing, mark it, and mark it with something that only it can carry. Sulphur marks protein. Phosphorus marks DNA.
